newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends lower, yields recent gains.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends lower, yields recent gains.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures finished sharply lower Monday, surrendering more than half of last week's gains, amid softening physical power and natural gas prices in the western U.S.
"It was overdone, and this is a correction," said one Houston marketer.
Electricity values at Palo Verde were especially pressured by returns of several coal and nuclear generating units.

The 1,080 megawatt (MW) unit 3 at the San Onofre nuclear generating station in San Clemente, Calif. reached full output over the weekend after reducing output after a control rod fell into the plant's reactor late Thursday.

The 1,221 MW Palo Verde 1 nuclear unit in Wintersburg, Ariz. was producing power almost 75 percent of capacity following its autumn refueling outage, and the 1,087 MW Diablo Canyon 1 nuclear plant in Avila Beach, Calif. was expected to return to full output some time today after scaling back operation for condenser cleaning over the weekend.
The 360 MW San Juan coal-fired unit 1 was back on line today after being shut early Thursday due to an ash builup.
December California-Oregon Border (COB) futures settled down $1.49 at $22.81 a megawatt hour (MWh), and touched interim support at $22.50, the session high of a week ago.
January COB finished down $2.17 at $20.52. Deferred COB months ended 60 cents to $2.00 lower.
December Palo Verde (PV) futures ended down $2.50 at $20.75, near its session low of $20.60. December PV almost filled a chart gap in the $20.50 and $21.00 range.
January PV also finished down $2.50 at $18.75. Other PV contracts ended 55 cents to $2.50 lower.
"It looks like temperatures are moderating everywhere," the Houston marketer. "There'll be more room on the downside."
NYMEX said 306 COB and 110 PV contracts were sold today.
